name: Homaranismo
summary: Homaranismo (Humanitism) is L. L. Zamenhof's ethical and quasi-religious philosophy of human fraternity, built on the golden rule and meant to give people of every religion and nationality a neutral common ground. It holds that all peoples are equal, that a country belongs equally to all its inhabitants, and that ethnic nationalism is group egoism to be outgrown, while each person keeps their own language, faith and family customs. It seeks gradual, unforced convergence, with a neutral language (Esperanto) in cross-group dealings, and says nothing about economic policy.
scope: The doctrine as Zamenhof set it out: the 1901 Russian 'Hillelism' (Dogmas of Hillelism) and the later Homaranismo declaration (1906 anonymous, 1913 under his name), as described by Wikipedia and Zamenhof's biography. Because it is an ethical-religious philosophy with no economic or institutional programme, most answers on economics and institutions are low-confidence inferences from its humanist principles. Excludes later Esperanto-movement politics (such as the Raumists or Esperanto's secular neutrality) and Baha'i interpretations by Lidia Zamenhof.

sources.usedFor: Describes Homaranism as a liberal, humanist quasi-religious doctrine of one human family, not anti-state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No wage policy is stated; the ideal of equal and absolute justice leans toward fairer pay, an inference only.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The doctrine has no economic content, so adherents are split or indifferent.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is outside the sources; personal conscience is stressed but no drug stance follows.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Dogma 2 calls persecuting people for birth into another race, language or religion barbarism, which supports restricting group-hatred, though no law is demanded.

state-harmful.rationale: Hillelism envisions states containing equal citizens and speaks of countries with equal rights, so it assumes a state rather than abolishing it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Dogma 6 wants public institutions to use neutral language and neutral or state festivals, so a larger public role for any one religion is opposed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Dogma 1 calls ethno-national goals group egoism that should fade, and Dogma 9 denies that national languages exist in any real sense.

gradual-change.rationale: The Essence stresses a gradual, unforced merging toward a human-neutral population, and Zamenhof describes no revolutionary programme.

nation-first.rationale: Zamenhof wrote in 1914 that all nationalism brings humanity great unhappiness, and Dogma 6 says serving only one group's interests is not patriotism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Dogma 7 treats all violence as violence even when the majority commits it, but intervention is never discussed.

central-planning.rationale: The doctrine has no economic programme.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is a fiscal detail the doctrine never touches.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy lies outside a doctrine about ethics, language and religion.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The distribution of property is not a subject in Zamenhof's texts.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dogma 7 demands equal rights for all citizens and Dogma 3 a state belonging to all inhabitants, which is incompatible with guided single-party rule.

direct-votes.rationale: Zamenhof wrote about equal rights, not the mechanics of lawmaking such as referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is a socialist idea the sources do not engage with.

natural-rulers.rationale: Dogma 2 holds all peoples equal and says people are judged by personal value and deeds, not origin.

political-violence-never.rationale: Dogma 7 calls violence by a group violence even when the majority commits it, yet no pacifist absolute is stated.

war-builds-character.rationale: Dogma 7 says equal rights will abolish the causes of all wars, so war is treated as an evil to remove.

separate-church-state.rationale: Dogma 6 calls for neutral language and neutral or state festivals in public institutions and Dogma 4 for neutral religious principles in dealings across groups.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Dogma 10 treats religious elements other than the golden rule and conscience as myths or customs that should give way to common human-neutral ones.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Dogma 3 states a country belongs equally to all inhabitants whatever their language or religion, and that tying national interests to one race is a relic of the rule of the fist and sword.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Dogma 7 demands equal justice and rights but not equal economic outcomes.

civilizational-union.rationale: Dogma 1 rejects group egoism along ethnic lines, and Hillelism wants merging across religions, not unions of co-religionists.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The core law of acting toward others as one wishes to be treated places other-regarding duty above pure self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The ethic stresses duties of fraternity, but equal rights are equally central; no ordering is stated.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is absent from the early-twentieth-century texts.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is never raised in the sources.

restore-past-order.rationale: Dogma 3 calls ethnic claims a leftover from an earlier age of force, and the movement looks forward to a human-neutral society.

means-match-ends.rationale: Dogma 7 treats violence as violence whoever commits it, and the doctrine aims at justice reached by just means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The doctrine envisions an advanced human community with a common neutral language, the opposite of primitivism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxian claims about profit are absent from the texts.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by one class over others conflicts with Dogma 3 and Dogma 7, which demand equal rights for every group within the state.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Zamenhof traces war to national and religious hatred and injustice, not to capitalism, but never discusses capitalism.

harm-principle.rationale: The sources set no general limit on state power beyond equal rights.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Dogma 4 and 6 let each group run its own schools and keep its language and faith, so group-linked cultural rights are accepted alongside individual equality.

state-as-business.rationale: The sources do not compare the state to a firm.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claims about media and universities are not made in the sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Dogma 2 holds peoples equal and judges individuals by personal value and deeds, not birth.

total-state.rationale: Hillelists leave family language and religion free (Dogma 4) and oppose imposing one's language or faith on others as barbarism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Dogma 1 calls ethnic national aims group egoism that should vanish and Zamenhof's 1914 letter called nationalism a source of unhappiness.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Dogma 5 forbids calling a foreign state or part of one's homeland one's own on ethnic grounds, and equal rights are meant to end the causes of war.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on personal oaths conflicts with a state of equal citizens under equal justice (Dogma 7).

bound-labor.rationale: Binding people to land and lord contradicts the equality and justice of Dogma 2 and Dogma 7.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The project of a human-neutral language and shared ethic assumes neutral common ground exists, an inference.

universal-morality.rationale: Dogma 10 makes the golden rule the fundamental law for all people across religious divisions, though it grounds it in God and conscience rather than reason alone.

single-common-good.rationale: Dogma 6 defines patriotism as serving the good of all citizens irrespective of group, a common good, though not through a rationalist theory.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zamenhof left Zionism, arguing in Hillelism that it would fail for lack of a common language, and opposed ethnic nationalism generally.

revive-national-language.rationale: Dogma 9 denies that national languages exist in any real sense and Dogma 6 wants a neutral language in public institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Zamenhof said all nationalism, of the strong and of the weak, brings unhappiness, and favoured equal rights within existing states over ethnic states.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dogma 10 keeps God, conscience and religious sentiment central, so reason is not the sole guide.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Dogma 2 calls persecution for birth into another race barbarism and Dogma 3 requires equal rights for all inhabitants.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Dogma 4 treats forcing one's language or religion on others as barbarism, and Dogma 6 wants equal treatment of all groups.

elite-replacement.rationale: The doctrine rejects hostile conspiracy thinking about ethnic groups, and Dogma 1 calls group hatred something to eliminate.

national-mission.rationale: Dogma 6 rejects serving one group's interests as patriotism and Zamenhof condemned nationalism of the strong as ignoble.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The texts contain no populist critique of elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Judging people by personal value and deeds (Dogma 2) and equal and absolute justice (Dogma 7) rule out coercive eugenics.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The stated aim of gradually merging into one human-neutral population and equality of races (Dogma 2) contradict it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Dogma 2 states that all peoples are equal and individuals are judged by personal value and deeds, and Dogma 7 requires equal and absolute justice.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate the sources do not touch.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Dogma 4 condemns forcing religion on others, and one cannot commend or condemn anyone for traditional religion, so legal restriction of conversion is alien.

population-transfer.rationale: Dogma 3 says a country belongs to all inhabitants with equal rights and Dogma 7 treats any group violence as violence, even when the majority commits it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Dogma 7 and the Essence see fraternity and equal justice, not struggle between peoples, as the path to human happiness.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British housing policy is far from the sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Hillelism rests on the view that peoples of different language and religion can live as equal citizens, and that conflict comes from injustice not diversity.

party-controls-media.rationale: Imposing one view on all conflicts with the stress on equal rights and with the condemnation of forcing language or religion on others.

clerical-rule.rationale: Dogma 10 treats most religious elements as customs and public life as neutral among religions, so clerical rule is opposed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources do not compare rural and urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Dogma 5 rejects claims to territory on ethnic grounds, which weighs against reunification of a divided nation as a goal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist views of graduates are absent from the texts.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Dogma 2 treats all peoples as equal and Dogma 4 respects each person's own language and faith, though the movement also wants customs to converge gradually.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Dogma 5 defines the fatherland as the state where one is born or lives, opposing descent-based ethnic claims.

minority-language-support.rationale: Dogma 7 calls for equal rights for all languages and Dogma 6 for each group to run its own schools.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Dogma 5 rejects claiming territory on ethnic or historical grounds, and equal rights are meant to end the causes of conflict.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Dogma 10 treats mythical religious elements as customs to fade and Dogma 2 holds all people equal by deeds.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Dogma 7 requires equal and absolute justice independent of strength, which leaves no place for a ruler above the law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not engaged by the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: The doctrine opposes ethnic or national glorification (Dogma 1, 6) and holds all people equal by personal value.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist-style question the sources never touch.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Dogma 5 says one may not call a foreign state or part of one's own homeland mine on ethnic grounds, which rejects such claims directly.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Dogma 4 condemns forcing religion on others and Dogma 10 treats religion as inherited and a matter of conscience.

women-must-cover.rationale: Imposed dress codes conflict with the condemnation of forcing faith on others and with freedom of conscience.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Dogma 1 rejects ethnic group goals and Dogma 5 rejects ethnic claims on territory, which weighs against unions of kin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Dogma 6 lets each group run its own schools, and Dogma 4 allows each group its own language and faith in family and group life.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Zamenhof left Zionism and held that equal rights for all in their country of residence is the path (Dogma 7), against founding an ethnic homeland.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Dogma 7 warns that majority-dominated states persecute defenders of equal rights and that majority violence is still violence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Dogma 2 says people are judged by personal value and deeds, not origin, which opposes inherited privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Dogma 2 holds all peoples equal and Dogma 4 condemns forcing one's language or religion on others.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Dogma 2 calls persecution for race, language or religion barbarism, which sits badly with a right to discriminate on any grounds.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Dogma 7 says defenders of equal rights will be persecuted and not be shaken, but violence is condemned, so resistance is not endorsed.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Hillelists are told to stay out of language and religion battles but to work for equal rights, so full withdrawal is not their stance.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of culture is not engaged.

native-born-offices.rationale: Dogma 3 and 5 define citizens by residence and equal rights for all inhabitants, not origin.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Dogma 5 rejects ethnic or historical claims over territory and Dogma 7 aims to end causes of wars.

single-official-language.rationale: Dogma 6 wants public institutions to use a neutral language but Dogma 7 gives equal rights to all languages and Dogma 4 forbids forcing language on others.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Dogma 7 calls any violence by one group against another violence and the aim is to end the causes of wars.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The doctrine rejects domination of one group over another and seeks to end the causes of wars.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The sources assume laws of equal justice but do not discuss obedience.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Dogmas 1 and 2 reject hatred of any group and persecution for birth, and Wikipedia says the doctrine answered antisemitic propaganda.

religious-nation.rationale: Dogma 3 says a country belongs to all inhabitants whatever their religion, and Dogma 4 condemns forcing religion on others.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The doctrine insists on equality among peoples (Dogma 2) and rejects dominance of the strong (Dogma 7).

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The doctrine has no property theory.

religion-illusion.rationale: Dogma 10 treats God as the highest Power and religion as a matter of conscience, with the golden rule as its core.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Historical judgment on capitalism is not given.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Dogma 9 denies national languages exist as such and Hillelism sought a neutral mixed language, not linguistic purity.

majority-settlement.rationale: Dogma 3 and 5 reject ethnic claims on regions, and Dogma 7 rejects majority domination of minorities.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Dogma 5 forbids calling territory mine on ethnic grounds and Zamenhof left Zionism, which rests on such a claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The doctrine opposes hatred of groups, and Zamenhof's children were murdered in the Holocaust (Wikipedia), though the event postdates his writings.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Dogma 7 demands equal rights and justice, and violence against dissent is violence.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Dogma 4 condemns forcing religion on others and Dogma 10 holds one cannot commend or condemn anyone for their religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Dogma 2 treats all peoples as equal, and domination for the benefit of one group is condemned as injustice.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious litmus tests for rulers contradict equal rights and the condemnation of forcing religion on others.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine claims neutral human ground between groups, but does not discuss left and right.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Dogma 10 says no one can be commended or condemned for their inherited religion, and religions are meant to meet on common ground.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Dogma 3 and 7 ground the state in the equal rights of its inhabitants, not in divine mandate.

property-franchise.rationale: Dogma 3 gives all inhabitants equal rights, which excludes wealth-based voting limits.

racial-franchise.rationale: Dogma 3 states a country belongs to all inhabitants with equal rights whatever their language or religion, and Dogma 2 rejects ranking by race.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Dogma 2 and 10 condemn persecution for religion and aim at merging across religions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Dogma 2 names persecution for birth into another race, language or religion as barbarism.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Dogma 10 says religious elements besides conscience and the golden rule are customs that should gradually yield to common human-neutral ones.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Dogma 10 keeps God and conscience and forbids imposing views on others, so state atheism is opposed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Dogma 7 requires equal rights for all communities and warns against majority domination.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources do not compare charity and welfare, though the ethic is charitable.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Nationalist drilled youth movements conflict with the rejection of ethnic national goals (Dogma 1, 6).

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Dogma 9 denies national languages in any real sense, and Dogma 1 treats ethnic national aims as group egoism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Glorifying death for the nation contradicts Dogma 1 and 6 and the aim to end war.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Zamenhof left Zionism, which sought a homeland, and favoured equal rights in each country of residence.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Dogma 3 and 7 give equal rights to all groups, and persecuting a group for birth is barbarism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Dogma 5 rejects drawing territory on ethnic lines.

person-over-state.rationale: The Essence stresses that each person keeps their homeland, language and religion on a neutral human basis, with equal justice for individuals.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Homaranismo is described as a moral and religious philosophy for uniting people, grounded in God as the highest power.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Dogma 1 calls group egoism along ethnic lines something to disappear, and Dogma 2 says persecuting someone for race is barbarism.

racial-pride.rationale: Dogma 8 says ethnic group is one's race and groups should avoid chauvinism, pride in group is not a value; Dogma 1 opposes group egoism.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Dogma 9 says Hillelists deny national languages exist in any real sense and Dogma 8 replaces nation with citizens of one fatherland.

communal-electorates.rationale: Dogma 3 gives all inhabitants equal rights as citizens and Dogma 6 wants neutral public institutions, which weighs against separate religious electorates.

arms-reduction.rationale: Dogma 7 aims at abolishing causes of wars and Zamenhof sought a world without war (Wikipedia), implying reduction of arms.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The doctrine works for equal rights within the existing state and not for its destruction (Dogma 3, 7).

sacred-nation.rationale: Dogma 1 calls ethnic national aims group egoism and human hatred, and Zamenhof wrote in 1914 that all nationalism brings great unhappiness.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Dogma 7 calls for equal rights for all religions, and Dogma 10 says no one can be commended or condemned for a traditional religion.

national-church-status.rationale: Zamenhof's scheme asks public institutions to be neutral among religions and ethnic groups, so no church gets a legal rank above others; this follows from the stated dogmas.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: It has no economic programme, so there is no basis for an answer.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: It has no economic programme, so there is no basis for an answer.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Its purpose is a neutral common ground for people of every religion, and it opposes politics divided along religious and national lines.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Zamenhof's texts address justice among peoples, not the distribution of wealth; no basis for a lean.

missingStatements.text: A neutral shared language should be used between peoples of different languages in order to reduce hatred between them.
missingStatements.rationale: Dogma 9 and Dogma 4 name a neutral language, currently Esperanto, as the basis for dealing across ethnic lines, and Zamenhof saw misunderstanding as a cause of hatred.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to constructed-language movements; few other ideologies take a side, so it would not earn a place in the bank.

missingStatements.text: Public institutions should use a language and festivals that are neutral among the state's ethnic and religious groups, while each group runs its own schools.
missingStatements.rationale: Dogma 6 sets out exactly this arrangement of neutral public institutions with separate group schools.

notes: Statements on economics and most institutional questions are not addressed by Zamenhof; they are low-confidence inferences or zero. Only the questions on nationalism, ethnic equality, religion, war and language have documented positions.
